chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Whoever preserves their forgetfulness (i.e., remembers they missed something) and completes it, then there is no Sajdat al-Sahw (prostrations of forgetfulness) upon them. For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed Dhuhr with the people for two rak'ahs, then he forgot. Dhu al-Shimalayn said to him, 'O Messenger of Allah, has something been revealed regarding the prayer?' He said, 'And what is that?' He said, 'You have only prayed two rak'ahs.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Do you say like his saying?' They said, 'Yes.' So he stood up and completed the prayer for them and performed the two prostrations of forgetfulness."

I (the narrator) said, 'What do you see regarding one who prayed two rak'ahs and thought they were four, then said the taslim and departed, then remembered after he had left that he had only prayed two rak'ahs?' He said, 'He faces the prayer from its beginning (i.e., starts a new prayer from the beginning).'

I said, 'Then why did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) not face the prayer (start anew), but rather completed what remained of his prayer?' He said, 'For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not leave his place. So if he did not leave his place, he should complete what was lacking from his prayer, provided he had preserved (remembered) the first two rak'ahs.'

key_terms.حَفِظَ سَهْوَهُ: Preserved/remembered one's forgetfulness (maintained awareness of the error)
key_terms.ذُو الشِّمَالَيْنِ: Dhu al-Shimalayn (a title for Abu Bakr, meaning 'Possessor of the Two Shoulders')
key_terms.سَجْدَتَا السَّهْوِ: Sajdat al-Sahw (the two prostrations of forgetfulness performed at the end of prayer)
key_terms.لَمْ يَبْرَحْ مِنْ مَجْلِسِهِ: Did not leave his place (remained in the spot where the prayer was performed)
key_terms.يَسْتَقْبِلُ الصَّلَاةَ: Faces the prayer (starts a new prayer from the beginning)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between completing a prayer and restarting it when one forgets the number of rak'ahs?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between *Sajdat al-Sahw* (prostrations of forgetfulness) and restarting prayer (*I'adat al-Salat*) based on whether the worshipper has physically left the prayer spot. It highlights the Prophet’s practical application of completing the prayer when remaining seated, a precedent that Shia scholars use to argue against the necessity of restarting for minor omissions if the physical location is retained. The narration further emphasizes the importance of preserving one's memory of the prayer structure (*hifz al-sahw*) to determine the correct corrective action.
